Check what stacking tables would do

Source: R/stack.R
sv_stack_check.Rd

Compares the columns of 2 to 8 tables and reports, column by column, what stacking them one under another would change: types that differ (and the type they would be cast to), values that become NA in a cast, labels that differ, columns missing from some tables, and near-miss names that differ only in case (these are never merged unless you ask with rename). Nothing is rounded or truncated silently: a cast converts a value exactly or gives NA, and the NA count says how many.

Usage

sv_stack_check(..., cast = NULL, rename = NULL)

Arguments

...

Two or more data frames. Unnamed tables are named by their expressions, as sideview() names them.

cast

Optional named character vector choosing a column's type, e.g. c(AGE = "chr"). Only an offered type is allowed.

rename

Optional named character vector merging a near-miss column into its partner, e.g. c(Age = "AGE"): the column Age is renamed AGE in every table that has it.

Value

An object of class sv_stack_check: the plan (inputs, id_col, n_rows, columns, kept_labels, tz), plus table (one row per column, with its type in each input and a Status), text (summary lines) and code.

Examples

wave1 <- data.frame(AGE = c(34, 51), SEX = c("F", "M"))
wave2 <- data.frame(Age = c("29", "40"), SEX = c("M", "M"))
sv_stack_check(wave1, wave2)
#> Stack 2 tables: 4 rows, 4 columns.
#> 1 near-miss name left apart.
#>  Column wave1 wave2                      Status
#>     AGE   num     - only in wave1 (NA in wave2)
#>     SEX   chr   chr                          ok
#>     Age     -   chr   near-miss for AGE? (case)
#> dplyr::bind_rows(wave1 = wave1, wave2 = wave2, .id = "source")
sv_stack_check(wave1, wave2, rename = c(Age = "AGE"))
#> Stack 2 tables: 4 rows, 3 columns.
#> 1 column changes type.
#>  Column wave1 wave2                       Status
#>     AGE   num   chr type differs -> as.character
#>     SEX   chr   chr                           ok
#> dplyr::bind_rows(wave1 = dplyr::mutate(wave1, AGE = as.character(AGE)), wave2 = dplyr::rename(wave2, AGE = Age), .id = "source")
